title: Rollforward-first rollback oracle for batch-cache autotune
creator: Aisha Kaplan
description: Build an automated acceptance and rollback oracle for applying batch/caching recommendations that prioritizes safe rollforward, minimizes false-positive rollbacks, and detects semantic regressions tied to cost optimizations. This ticket implements a lightweight eval harness that runs during canary/apply windows: shadow traffic replay, golden-anchor scoring, stratified synthetic perturbations, and a statistical decision layer that outputs one of: APPLY, ROLLFORWARD_WITH_MONITORING, or ROLLBACK. The goal is to enable automated config apply for low-risk cases while guaranteeing human-in-the-loop escalation for ambiguous regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Eval harness runs as part of config apply pipeline and finishes within 10 minutes for typical canary size
Golden-anchor suite with at least 200 prompts per high-risk customer surface and pass/fail scoring available
Decision layer implements paired nonparametric test + pragmatic effect size threshold and produces a deterministic action (APPLY / ROLLFORWARD_WITH_MONITORING / ROLLBACK)
Automated rollback runbook triggers a canary unwind action within 2 minutes of ROLLBACK decision and posts incident ticket with failing metrics
Dashboard shows per-canary behavior: latency, token-cost delta, semantic-fidelity delta, and a scalar acceptance score
tasks: Design graded acceptance metric (composite of semantic fidelity, perplexity shift, and response-length drift)
Implement golden-anchor selector service that picks 3 anchor sets per customer: core, edge, and adversarial
Integrate shadow-replay runner to drive the autotune candidate configs against production-like requests
Add statistical decision engine: paired bootstrap + Cliff's delta for effect sizing
Wire the decision output to rollout controller to execute APPLY / ROLLFORWARD_WITH_MONITORING / ROLLBACK
Create dashboard slices and alerts for human review and postmortem data retention
Write integration tests and small-scale canary test in staging; attach PRs
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Kaplan: Initial ticket created after spike showing some autotune candidates caused subtle semantic drift for inflection prompts. Goal: enable safe automation for low-risk candidates.

2025-02-14 - Marco Reyes: Spike results in /tmp showed bootstrap CI gives wide intervals on small golden sets. Proposal: stratified sampling + synthetic perturbations to amplify sensitivity for adversarial cases.
2025-02-16 - Nivedita Shah (PM): Prioritize rollforward-first behavior to avoid unnecessary customer impact for borderline signals. Add a monitoring window step when signal is ambiguous.
2025-02-18 - Design review comment (Luca Moretti): Suggest visual indicator in console that shows which prompts contributed most to failure score (heatmap).

2025-02-20 - Marco Reyes: Implemented prototype decision engine in feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3284 (unit tests + basic harness). Needs integration with rollout controller and dashboard.
2025-02-20 - Aisha Kaplan: Flagging dependency on ENG-42877 for improved KV-cache instrumentation to compute semantic-fidelity deltas reliably.
decision_log: 2025-02-15 - Decision: Use a composite acceptance score instead of single-metric gating to reduce sensitivity to noise in any one metric
2025-02-17 - Decision: Rollforward-first policy for borderline scores (apply with 24h monitoring) to reduce unnecessary disruption; only immediate rollback on strong negative signal
2025-02-19 - Decision: Require at least one adversarial-anchor failure to trigger human escalation regardless of composite score
implementation_notes: Prototype uses a paired bootstrap over response embeddings (cosine similarity) + normalized token-cost delta to compute composite score
Golden anchors will be persisted per-customer and versioned; we will store a light fingerprint for quick similarity checks before running full harness
Monitoring window uses progressive thresholds: 1h fast-alert (high sensitivity), 24h stability check (low false-positive tolerance)
